subject: Music Production
title: Amplitude and Loudness
description: Learn Amplitude and Loudness in one minute.

hook.text: When you hit a drum softly, the head barely moves and the sound is quiet.

buildup.text: Striking harder makes the drum head move further, pushing bigger waves of air pressure outward.

discovery.text: The size of these pressure waves is called amplitude, and our ears perceive it as loudness.

twist.text: Loudness is measured in decibels on a logarithmic scale, so ten decibels sounds twice as loud.

climax.text: Producers carefully manage amplitude to prevent distortion and keep mixes balanced.

punchline.text: Volume is just how far the air molecules swing.

quiz.question: What does amplitude determine about a sound?
